steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch and airplane mode
steps.detail: Make sure the laptop's Wi-Fi switch or function key is on and airplane mode is off. Look for the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar to confirm it is connected.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin the Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Open the Wi-Fi settings, select the network, choose Forget, then select it again and enter the Wi-Fi password. This creates a fresh connection profile.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update or the software update settings and install any available updates, including network driver updates. Restart if asked.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. This clears temporary network problems and lets the Wi-Fi connection set up again.

steps.title: Check the printer is powered on and connected
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display and make sure it is turned on and not showing an error. Check that the network or USB cable is pushed firmly into both the printer and the computer.

steps.title: Check the printer queue for stuck jobs
steps.detail: Open the printers settings on your computer and select the office printer to see whether a document is stuck in the queue. Cancel any stuck jobs if you can see them.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on
steps.detail: Switch the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, and switch it back on. Give it a minute or two to finish starting up before trying again.

steps.title: Restart your computer
steps.detail: Restart your computer so it reconnects to the printer. Then check whether the printer shows as online.

steps.detail: An orange blinking light often means the printer is out of paper, even if the tray looks empty. Load paper into the tray and slide the guides snug against the edges.

steps.title: Check the power and cable connections
steps.detail: Make sure the power cord is firmly plugged into the printer and the outlet. If the printer connects by USB or network cable, check that the cable is pushed all the way in at both ends.

steps.title: Check the print queue
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to Bluetooth & devices, then Printers & scanners, and select your printer. Open the queue to see whether any jobs are stuck waiting.

steps.title: Restart the printer
steps.detail: Turn the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, and turn it back on. Give it a few minutes to warm up and finish its startup checks, then try printing a test page.

steps.title: Unplug and plug back in headphones or USB audio

steps.title: Check the printer for paper, toner and error lights
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or lights for warnings such as no paper, low toner or a paper jam. Fill the paper tray or clear any jam you can reach easily.

steps.title: Check the printer's cable or Wi-Fi connection
steps.detail: If the printer uses a USB cable, make sure both ends are firmly plugged in. If it connects over Wi-Fi, check that its display shows it is connected.

steps.title: Print to a different printer for now
steps.detail: If another printer is nearby, send your document to it so you can keep working. Choose the other printer from the printer list in the Print window.

steps.title: Cancel the stuck job and send it again
steps.detail: Open the printer queue from the Print window or the printer's icon in Settings. Select the stuck job, choose Cancel, and then send your document again.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on
steps.detail: Switch the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, and switch it on again. Wait until it shows ready before you try printing.

steps.title: Restart the computer and try again
steps.detail: Restart your computer from the Start menu. After it starts, send your document to the printer again.

steps.detail: Remove the headset from its USB port, wait a few seconds, then push it firmly into the same port or a different one. Make sure the plug is fully seated.

steps.title: Set the headset as the default playback device
steps.detail: Click the speaker icon in the taskbar, open the sound output menu, and select the USB headset from the list. Sound should switch to the headset.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your open work, then restart the computer. After it starts up, plug in the headset and check whether the sound plays through it.

steps.detail: If you use a headset or external microphone, make sure its plug is pushed fully into the correct port. Try a different port if you have one.

steps.detail: Unplug your USB headset or microphone, wait a few seconds, and plug it back in. Then check whether Teams picks it up.

steps.detail: Make sure the cable is pushed fully into the monitor and into the laptop's video port or adapter. Look for a loose connection.

steps.title: Select the correct input on the monitor
steps.detail: Use the monitor's buttons or menu to switch to the input that matches the port you're using, such as HDMI or DisplayPort. Wait a few seconds after switching.

steps.title: Unplug and plug back in the monitor cable
steps.detail: Disconnect the cable from the laptop or adapter, wait about 10 seconds, then reconnect it firmly. Check whether the monitor picks up the signal.

steps.title: Detect the display in system settings
steps.detail: On Windows, open Settings > System > Display and select Detect. On a Mac, open System Settings > Displays and check that the external monitor is listed.

steps.title: Restart the laptop with the monitor connected
steps.detail: Save your work, restart the laptop, and leave the monitor plugged in during startup. Check whether the external display shows an image afterward.

steps.title: Check the camera cover or privacy shutter
steps.detail: Look at the top of the screen for a small sliding cover or switch over the camera. Slide it open if it is closed.

steps.title: Close and reopen the video call app
steps.detail: Quit the app you use for video calls completely, then open it again. Join the call once more and check whether the picture appears.

steps.title: Try the call in another browser
steps.detail: If you join calls through a web browser, open a different browser and join the call there. If the picture works, the first browser is the problem.

steps.title: Close other apps that may use the camera
steps.detail: Close any other apps that could be using the camera, such as a photo or recording app. Then return to your video call and check the picture.

steps.title: Check the app's camera permission
steps.detail: Open the device's privacy settings and find the Camera section. Make sure the video call app is allowed to use the camera.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. After it starts again, open your video call app and check the camera.

steps.detail: Look for the sun-shaped brightness keys on the keyboard, often on the function row. Press the brightness up key a few times and see if the screen gets brighter.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop from the Start menu. Once it starts back up, check whether the screen is bright again.

steps.title: Turn off Caps Lock and retype your password
steps.detail: The light on your keyboard is probably Caps Lock, which makes passwords fail. Press the Caps Lock key once to turn it off, then type your password again.

steps.title: Check the keyboard language
steps.detail: Look at the language indicator on the sign-in screen or taskbar. If it shows a language other than the one you normally use, switch to yours and type the password again.

steps.title: Check Num Lock and the keyboard layout
steps.detail: Make sure Num Lock is set the way you expect, since number keys can behave differently. Then type the password slowly, watching the characters on screen as you go.

steps.title: Use the normal password reset page
steps.detail: If the password still fails, open the standard password reset page from the sign-in screen or your organization's sign-in website. Follow the prompts to set a new password, then sign in with it.

steps.title: Try the portal in another browser
steps.detail: Open the company portal address in Microsoft Edge or Firefox. If it loads correctly there, you can keep working in that browser while the Chrome problem is looked at.

steps.title: Close and reopen Chrome
steps.detail: Close every Chrome window, then open Chrome again and load the company portal. This clears up many temporary page problems.

steps.title: Clear the Chrome browser cache
steps.detail: Open Chrome settings, go to Privacy and security, choose Clear browsing data, select cached images and files, and clear them. Then reload the portal.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Chrome's menu, choose Help, then About Google Chrome, and let it check for and install any update. Restart Chrome when it asks, then try the portal again.

steps.title: Restart the computer

steps.title: Close and reopen Edge

steps.title: Restart Outlook
steps.detail: Close Outlook completely, then open it again. Wait a moment for it to connect and check whether new emails arrive.

steps.title: Restart your computer
steps.detail: Save your open work, restart the computer, and then open Outlook again to see whether it connects and shows new email.

steps.title: Wait a minute for Excel to recover
steps.detail: Excel sometimes needs a short time to finish a calculation. Give it about a minute before doing anything else.

steps.title: Close Excel from Task Manager
steps.detail: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager, select Microsoft Excel, and choose End task. Then reopen Excel.

steps.title: Reopen the spreadsheet and check recent versions
steps.detail: Open Excel again and use File > Open > Recent to find the spreadsheet. Excel may offer to recover the unsaved version when it restarts.

steps.title: Install pending Office updates
steps.detail: Open Excel, go to File > Account, and choose Update Options > Update Now. Restart Excel after the update finishes.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save any other open work, then restart the computer to clear memory and any stuck programs. Open Excel again after it starts up.

steps.detail: Open a website in your web browser, such as a news site. If it does not load, check that the Wi-Fi is on and reconnect to your network.

steps.detail: Go to teams.microsoft.com in your web browser and sign in. This lets you keep working while the desktop app is being fixed.

steps.title: Quit and reopen Microsoft Teams
steps.detail: Close Microsoft Teams completely, including from the system tray or menu bar, then open it again. Wait a minute for it to load.

steps.title: Turn Wi-Fi off and on
steps.detail: Turn off Wi-Fi on your computer, wait about 10 seconds, then turn it back on. Wait for the connection to return before opening Teams.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update or the Microsoft Store and install any available updates for Microsoft Teams. Restart Teams after the update finishes.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer. Open Teams again once it has started.

steps.detail: Look through your open tabs and close the ones you no longer need. Keeping fewer tabs open frees up memory so the laptop can respond faster.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. A restart clears temporary memory use and often brings back normal speed.

steps.title: Check the charger cable at both ends
steps.detail: Make sure the cable is pushed firmly into the laptop and into the power brick. Look at the plug on the wall side too, and confirm it is fully inserted.

steps.title: Try a different wall outlet
steps.detail: Plug the charger straight into a different wall socket that you know has power, such as one where you've charged a phone. This rules out a dead outlet.

steps.title: Check the power strip switch
steps.detail: If the charger is plugged into a power strip or surge protector, make sure it is switched on and its light is lit. Plugging straight into a wall socket also helps you test this.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: With the charger connected, shut the laptop down completely and turn it back on. Then check whether the charging light comes on.

steps.title: Lower the speaker volume
steps.detail: Turn your computer's speaker volume down a little while you are on the call. Sound from the speakers can get picked up by your microphone and repeated back to others.

steps.title: Use headphones or earbuds
steps.detail: Plug in headphones or earbuds, or use a Bluetooth headset if you have one. This keeps the sound from your speakers out of your microphone.

steps.title: Restart Zoom
steps.detail: Close the Zoom app completely, then open it again and join the call. This can clear a sound problem that started inside the app.

steps.title: Check the Zoom audio settings
steps.detail: In Zoom, open Settings, then Audio. Make sure the correct microphone and speaker are selected, and use the test options to check how you sound.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Restart your computer, then open Zoom and join a test meeting to see if the echo is gone.

steps.title: Press a key or move the mouse
steps.detail: Tap the Shift key or move the touchpad once. This often wakes a laptop that has gone to sleep.

steps.title: Check the screen brightness keys
steps.detail: Press the brightness-up key on the keyboard, usually marked with a sun icon. The screen may be on but turned all the way down.

steps.title: Check the power adapter
steps.detail: Make sure the charger is plugged into the laptop and the wall outlet, and that the outlet has power. Then wait a moment and press a key again.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Close the lid, wait ten seconds, and open it again. If the screen is still black, press the power button once and wait two minutes for the laptop to start up.

steps.title: Remove and pair the headphones again

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Restart the laptop from the Start menu, then turn the headphones on and try connecting again.
